title: Design System: Workdash — Landing surface (the crew board)

scope.boundary: The application (/app) keeps the incumbent cozy gamer den system (--wd-* tokens, three-column desk shell). No --brd-* token appears inside /app; no --wd-* token appears on /. DESIGN.md documents both, the den system first and this surface-scoped world second.

frontmatter.name: Workdash — Crew Board (landing surface)
frontmatter.description: A night-shift roster board in enamelled steel; the board never themes, only the wall behind it does.

lamp-amber.purpose: A station in the voice call. Also the pushbutton, focus ring, caret and selection.

lens-green.purpose: A station in the world but not in the call. The second and last lamp colour.

signal.purpose: Destructive text only (sign out). Not a lamp state; must never be used as one.

enamel.purpose: The board field. Fixed material; never themed.

alu.purpose: Edge banding, bezels, lamp housings, screw heads, ghost stroke, scrollbar thumb.

plate.purpose: Name plates riding in routed channels; engraved in Legend Black.

ink.purpose: Type on enamel. Fixed; it is --brd-ink* and never follows the theme.

wall-light.purpose: The wall the board hangs on, light theme. The only layer that themes.

wall-dark.purpose: The wall the board hangs on, dark theme.

display.purpose: The single page headline. Width axis 94%.

body.purpose: All prose, measure capped at 68ch (58ch / 34ch in narrower columns).

plate.purpose: Engraved names on bone laminate. Width axis 90% is what makes a plate read as a plate.

legend.purpose: Uppercase signage labels: column headers, lamp states, spec fields, nav links. Never a kicker, never a sentence.

ledger.purpose: The paper strip, time-on readouts, footer, captions. Always tabular numerals.

shadows.purpose: Laminate sitting in a channel: lit top edge, dark bottom edge, its own cast.

motion.name: wd-board-seat
motion.purpose: Plates slide home in their channels. Position only — opacity is never animated from zero, so the name is legible in the first frame.

motion.name: wd-lamp-warm
motion.purpose: A filament curve: glow, surge, dip, settle. Not a cross-fade.

motion.name: lamp-delay
motion.purpose: The single stagger both the plate seat and the lamp warm-up read from.

motion.name: lens-transition
motion.purpose: Lens state change once the board is lit.

motion.name: pool-transition
motion.purpose: Lamplight pooling on the enamel behind a lit station.

motion.name: button-press
motion.value: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.25, 1), box-shadow 120ms ease, filter 160ms ease

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) — wd-board-seat and wd-lamp-warm set to none; button, lens and pool transitions collapse to 1ms with zero delay; smooth scrolling off
motion.purpose: The board simply starts lit. Mandatory for any new motion on this surface.

caveats.name: aluminium-band-periods
caveats.body: The brushed band uses three repeating gradients at 3px, 7px and 13px. They are not effectively incommensurate: measurement shows a dominant 21px repeat and the 13px layer inert at this scale. It reads as brushed metal only because the band is 2px tall at roughly 9% modulation. Re-derive the periods before changing that band's height or contrast.

narrative.overview:
A roster board in enamelled steel, hung on a wall. Deep bottle-green enamel field, brushed-aluminium edge banding and screw heads, bone-laminate name plates riding in routed channels, domed lamps in aluminium housings, and a paper ledger strip clipped along the bottom. Presence is not a feature bullet here; it is a physical fact you read off the board. Four lamps lit means four people are in the room right now.

The board is one object under one light, so it is made of fixed material and never themes. Only the wall it hangs on follows the app's light/dark setting. Lamplight is the only chroma in the palette: amber for in-call, green lens for in-world, dark for absent. Everything else is enamel, aluminium, bone laminate and paper.
keyCharacteristics: Theme-invariant object on a theme-following wall
One working ink plus lamp light; no decorative colour
Depth built from separated physical layers, never from a drop shadow alone
Engraved signage lettering, width axis carrying the register
Exactly one authored motion moment, on first paint only

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Amber and green are lamp states, not a palette. No surface, border, illustration or decoration on this route may carry chroma that is not light coming from a lamp.

rules.name: The Two Families Rule
rules.body: --brd-ink* is the board's fixed ink and never changes with the theme. --brd-fg* is ink on the current surface, and it is redefined per surface: html:has(.wd-board-page) sets it to wall ink and flips it under .dark; .wd-board, .wd-board-window and .wd-board-rail re-point it at --brd-ink*; .wd-board-paper re-points it at its own darker paper ink. This is the single most important rule in the system.

rules.name: The Board Does Not Theme Rule
rules.body: Adding a new board surface means declaring its ink family, not adding a .dark variant. .dark may only change the wall.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Register Rule
rules.body: Register is set with font-stretch, not with a second family and not with a size bump: 94% display, 96% head, 90% plate, 86% legend.

rules.name: The Legend Is A Label Rule
rules.body: The uppercase letterspaced signage voice names a thing that exists — a column, a state, a spec field, a destination. It is never set above a headline as a kicker or eyebrow, and never used for a sentence.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes over time is set in tabular numerals so the column does not twitch.

rules.name: The Two-Sided Edge Rule
rules.body: Every raised or recessed element carries a lit edge and a shaded edge from the same light. A single flat shadow is not depth here.

rules.name: The Light Reaches The Wall Rule
rules.body: A lit board throws light, not just shadow. Any new board-class surface carries --brd-spill-glow in its shadow stack or it looks pasted on.

rules.name: The Never From Zero Rule
rules.body: The plate animation moves position only. Opacity is never animated from 0: the name is legible in the first frame, with or without motion.

dos: Do write var(--brd-fg) / --brd-fg-dim / --brd-fg-faint for text and let the surface decide the ink, and do declare the full --brd-fg* + --brd-hairline + --brd-lamp-ink set on any new board-class surface.
Do build depth from a lit edge, a shaded edge and a real cast — .wd-board-mount wrapping .wd-board with .wd-board-frame is the whole pattern.
Do set register with font-stretch on the 86/90/94/96% ramp.
Do keep every board radius in the 3–7px machined range and every circle a real circle.
Do duplicate any lamp state in text for screen readers and keep every readout in tabular numerals.
Do gate any new motion on prefers-reduced-motion and animate from an already-legible state.
donts: Don't add a .dark variant to the board. Only the wall themes.
Don't introduce a third lamp colour or any chroma that is not lamplight — no brand purple, no den amber from --wd-*, no status palette.
Don't use the uppercase legend voice as a kicker or eyebrow above a heading, and don't set a sentence in it.
Don't put --brd-* tokens inside /app or --wd-* tokens on /.

Don't replace a built layer with a blur — no accent blobs, no backdrop-filter glass, no blurred gradient behind the board. The spill glow is the board's own silhouette and nothing else fills that role.
Don't wrap the product screenshot in mock browser chrome or a floating card; it is a cut-out in the enamel.
Don't add a second type family. Archivo's width axis is the second family.
